if only…! that would be great!

Although she was exhausted, Giulia was smiling.
To form the congiuntivo imperfetto of regular verbs: parlassi, credessi, partissi.
To learn the irregular forms: fossi, dessi, stessi, facessi, dicessi, bevessi.
To apply the sequence of tenses: Penso che sia… → Pensavo che fosse…
To use "come se" + congiuntivo imperfetto: come se fosse napoletana.
To express a wish with "magari" + congiuntivo imperfetto: Magari potessi!
To describe an unexpected day and a birth.
Florence, 17th May, six in the morning. Graziella and Pietro hurry into the hospital's maternity ward. Matei is waiting for them in the corridor, unshaven, red-eyed and with a huge smile.
She's born! At twenty past four this morning.
Already? But I thought she was due on the twentieth!
So did I — I thought we still had three days. My parents have been on the train since yesterday: I was hoping they'd arrive in time.
You said "she"! So it's a girl! It's Viola, isn't it? It's Viola!
Viola? Pietro, how do you know?
Er… I didn't know. I guessed. As if I were a magician.
(laughs) Yes, it's Viola. The doctor wanted Giulia to sleep, but she wanted me to open the envelope straight away, even though we both knew what it said.
And what's she like? Tell me everything!
She's tiny: two kilos nine hundred. She has black hair, as if she were a hundred per cent Neapolitan. And she looks at everything with wide-open eyes, as if she wanted to restore the ceiling.
Can I see her? If only I could hold her!
The midwife asked us to go in one at a time and not to make any noise.
Then you go first, Pietro. But wash your hands first. And if you cry, don't worry: I'll be crying too.
"come se fossi" = as if I were
"uno alla volta" = one at a time
Double SS, stress on "FOS": FOS-see, FOS-se. Don't confuse it with "fosse" = ditches!
Stress on "LAS": par-LAS-see, par-LAS-se-ro. In the plural the stress is still on "LAS"!
It's formed from the verb stem + -assi (-are verbs), -essi (-ere), -issi (-ire). It's very regular:
The "io" and "tu" forms are identical. That's why the pronoun is often added: "Voleva che io venissi", "Voleva che tu venissi".
"Avere" is regular (avessi). "Fare", "dire", "bere" use the old Latin stem: FACere → facessi, DICere → dicessi, BEVere → bevessi.
If the main verb (penso, voglio, spero) moves into the PAST or the conditional, the present subjunctive becomes the IMPERFECT subjunctive:
Il medico vuole che Giulia dorma.
Il medico voleva che Giulia dormisse.
English also shifts the tense ("I think it IS" → "I thought it WAS"). In Italian the subjunctive shifts too: "pensavo che FOSSE", NOT "pensavo che sia". This is the most important rule of level B1!
Also after the conditional: "Vorrei che tu venissi" (I'd like you to come). "Sarebbe bello che restassi" (It would be nice if you stayed).
"Come se" (as if) ALWAYS takes the congiuntivo imperfetto (or trapassato), even when the main verb is in the present:
She has black hair, as if she were Neapolitan.
He looks at me as if he knew me.
She talks as if she were a hundred years old.
NOT "come se è" and NOT "come se sarebbe". Always: come se FOSSE.
"Magari!" on its own means "That would be great!". Followed by the congiuntivo imperfetto it expresses a strong wish, often one that's hard to fulfil:
Are you coming to Sibiu with us? — I wish!
Careful: "magari" + indicative = "maybe": "Magari domani piove" (Maybe it'll rain tomorrow). With the congiuntivo imperfetto = a wish.

If only it would rain tomorrow!

I was hoping they'd arrive in time.

Everyone thought Viola would be born on the twentieth of May, as Dr Ricci had said. Ion and Doina had planned the journey so that they would arrive in Florence on the seventeenth, three days early. Ion had calculated everything: four trains, three connections, twenty-six hours. "It would be impossible for a baby to be born before a train arrives," he had said. He was wrong.

On the evening of the sixteenth Giulia and Matei were having dinner at Graziella's. Giulia had just finished a plate of pappardelle when she put down her fork. "Matei," she said calmly, as if she were talking about the weather. "I think we ought to go to the hospital." Matei got up so fast that he knocked over two glasses and a chair. Graziella, on the other hand, picked up the bag Giulia had packed a month earlier and was already at the door.

At that moment Ion and Doina were on the night train between Budapest and Vienna. Doina was knitting, Ion was asleep. At half past eleven Doina's phone vibrated. It was a message from Matei: "We're at the hospital. Don't worry." Doina woke Ion. Ion looked at the message, then at the train timetable, then at the message again, as if he could change the timetable just by looking at it.

For the first time in forty years, Ion went to find the guard and asked him, in terrible German, whether the train could go faster. The guard, an Austrian with a white moustache, looked at him as if he were mad. Then he understood. He shook his hand, took a little bottle of grappa out of his pocket and said the only Romanian word he knew: "Noroc!"

At the hospital the night was long. Matei walked up and down the corridor until the midwife asked him to sit down, because he was wearing out the floor. Graziella sat on a plastic chair with her rosary in her hand, although she hadn't been to church for years. Pietro was asleep at home with Signor Franco, after making them swear they would wake him "as soon as something happened".

At twenty past four in the morning a door opened and the midwife called Matei. He went in as if he were walking on water. Giulia was in bed, pale, her hair damp, holding a little white bundle. She smiled. "Come," she said softly. "Come and meet your daughter." Matei looked at Ion's watch, which he had been carrying in his pocket for a week: twenty past four. It hadn't lost a single minute.

The baby was tiny, with a head full of black hair and two minuscule hands that opened and closed as if they were looking for something in the air. When Matei took her in his arms, she opened her eyes. They were dark and deep, and they looked at him with incredible seriousness, as if she wanted to understand who this man was who was crying and laughing at the same time.

"Shall we open the envelope?" asked Giulia. Matei laughed. "We already know what it says." "I know. But I want us to open it anyway. I've waited five months." Matei had brought the envelope to the hospital in the bag, together with Ernesto's small brush. He opened it carefully, as if it were a Renaissance document. Inside, in Giulia's handwriting, it said: "If it's a girl: Viola."

Ion and Doina arrived at Santa Maria Novella station on the seventeenth, at eight in the evening, ten minutes late. This time Ion didn't complain. He ran to a taxi, gave the hospital address and told the driver, in Romanian, that if he drove fast he'd give him a bottle of pălincă. The driver didn't understand a word, but drove very fast anyway.

Doina took Viola in her arms and looked at her for a long time without speaking. Then she said something in Romanian, so softly that only Matei heard it: "Are ochii mamei." She has my mother's eyes. Matei looked at the baby, then at his mother, and thought of the portrait with the blue veil. If only Grandma Viorica could see her, he thought. But perhaps, in a way, she could.

The last to arrive, on the morning of the eighteenth, was Professor Bellini. He was holding a bunch of violets. "How did you know the name, Professor?" asked Giulia, astonished. "I didn't," he replied. "But yesterday I asked Pietro whether it was a boy or a girl, and he went as red as a tomato and said: 'I can't tell you anything, I promised.' So I realised there was a secret. And a secret, in this family, is always something beautiful."

Then he went over to the cot and looked at Viola for a long moment, with his hands behind his back, the way he looked at paintings. "Look," he told her softly. "And don't touch anything." Viola, as if she had understood, closed her eyes and fell asleep.
"sarebbe nata" = would be born (future in the past)
"perché arrivassero" = so that they would arrive
"come se parlasse" = as if she were talking
"come se avesse capito" = as if she had understood

The announcement Matei and Giulia sent to their friends. Read and answer.
With immense joy we announce the birth of Viola Popa Esposito, born in Florence on 17th May at 4.20.
She weighs 2.9 kilos and has more hair than her father. We thought she'd arrive on the 20th, but she was in a hurry.
We thank the midwife Paola and Dr Ricci, who were as patient as if they were two grandmothers.
Mother and baby are doing very well. Dad a little less so: he hasn't slept for three nights.
"aveva fretta" = she was in a hurry
Un po’ meno bene: non dorme

My sister wanted me to go to the supermarket with her, but it was an excuse.
When I got back, all my friends were in the living room, as if it were a surprise party… because it was!
